questions.title: Library reminders
questions.stimulus:
A local library stores details of its members and their loans in a relational database. The contents of the Members and Loans tables are shown.

**Members**

| MemberID | Name | Suburb |
|---|---|---|
| M01 | Ava Chen | Hornsby |
| M02 | Liam Patel | Epping |
| M03 | Noah Kim | Hornsby |
| M04 | Zara Ali | Hornsby |
| M05 | Ethan Brown | Epping |

**Loans**

| LoanID | MemberID | BookTitle | LoanDate | Returned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L01 | M01 | Dune | 2025-02-11 | No |
| L02 | M02 | Holes | 2025-03-02 | No |
| L03 | M03 | Wonder | 2024-11-20 | No |
| L04 | M04 | Matilda | 2025-05-14 | Yes |
| L05 | M04 | Coraline | 2025-06-01 | No |
| L06 | M05 | Hatchet | 2025-01-09 | No |
| L07 | M03 | Holes | 2025-07-30 | No |

parts.prompt:
The library wants to send reminders to members who live in Hornsby and still have a book that was borrowed in 2025 and has not been returned.

Write an SQL query to display the member names and book titles for these loans, in alphabetical order by member name.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct SQL query with at least TWO of the following: joining the tables; all three conditions (Hornsby, not returned, borrowed in 2025); correct ordering
Shows some understanding of joining the tables or filtering

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Members.Name, Loans.BookTitle
FROM Members, Loans
WHERE Members.MemberID = Loans.MemberID
  AND Members.Suburb = 'Hornsby'
  AND Loans.Returned = 'No'
  AND Loans.LoanDate >= '2025-01-01' AND Loans.LoanDate <= '2025-12-31'
ORDER BY Members.Name ASC
```

Result:

| Name | BookTitle |
|---|---|
| Ava Chen | Dune |
| Noah Kim | Holes |
| Zara Ali | Coraline |

Traps: Noah Kim's 'Wonder' is unreturned but borrowed in 2024; Zara Ali's 'Matilda' was returned.

questions.title: Gym visits (reading)
questions.stimulus:
A gym records every class booking in the Sessions table. Minutes is the length of the class. The contents of the Sessions table are shown.

**Sessions**

| SessionID | MemberName | Class | Minutes | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Ana | Yoga | 60 | Attended |
| S02 | Ben | Spin | 45 | Attended |
| S03 | Cal | Yoga | 60 | Cancelled |
| S04 | Ana | Boxing | 50 | Attended |
| S05 | Dev | Spin | 45 | Attended |
| S06 | Ben | Yoga | 60 | Attended |
| S07 | Cal | Spin | 45 | Cancelled |
| S08 | Eve | Boxing | 50 | Attended |
| S09 | Dev | Boxing | 50 | Attended |

parts.prompt:
The following SQL query is run on the Sessions table.

```
SELECT MemberName, COUNT(SessionID) AS Visits
FROM Sessions
WHERE Minutes >= 50 AND Status = 'Attended'
GROUP BY MemberName
ORDER BY MemberName DESC
```

Type the table of results produced by the query, with its column headings.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides the correct output, including the column headings and the correct ordering of the rows
Provides some correct rows OR correct rows in the wrong order

parts.sample_answer:
| MemberName | Visits |
|---|---|
| Eve | 1 |
| Dev | 1 |
| Ben | 1 |
| Ana | 2 |

Traps: >= 50 includes the 50-minute Boxing classes; DESC sorts names Z→A; Cal has no attended sessions so does not appear.

questions.title: Gym class report
questions.stimulus:
A gym records every class booking in the Sessions table. Minutes is the length of the class. The contents of the Sessions table are shown.

**Sessions**

| SessionID | MemberName | Class | Minutes | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Ana | Yoga | 60 | Attended |
| S02 | Ben | Spin | 45 | Attended |
| S03 | Cal | Yoga | 60 | Cancelled |
| S04 | Ana | Boxing | 50 | Attended |
| S05 | Dev | Spin | 45 | Attended |
| S06 | Ben | Yoga | 60 | Attended |
| S07 | Cal | Spin | 45 | Cancelled |
| S08 | Eve | Boxing | 50 | Attended |
| S09 | Dev | Boxing | 50 | Attended |

parts.prompt:
Construct a SQL query that displays, for each class:

- the class name
- the number of sessions attended, with the heading Attended
- the total minutes attended, with the heading TotalMinutes

Cancelled sessions must not be counted. List the results from the highest to the lowest total minutes.

question.dataset_setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE Sessions (SessionID TEXT PRIMARY KEY, MemberName TEXT, Class TEXT, Minutes INTEGER, Status TEXT);
INSERT INTO Sessions VALUES ('S01','Ana','Yoga',60,'Attended'),('S02','Ben','Spin',45,'Attended'),('S03','Cal','Yoga',60,'Cancelled'),('S04','Ana','Boxing',50,'Attended'),('S05','Dev','Spin',45,'Attended'),('S06','Ben','Yoga',60,'Attended'),('S07','Cal','Spin',45,'Cancelled'),('S08','Eve','Boxing',50,'Attended'),('S09','Dev','Boxing',50,'Attended');

marking_criteria.criterion: 1 mark each: COUNT and SUM with the AS headings; WHERE excludes cancelled sessions; GROUP BY Class; ORDER BY TotalMinutes DESC

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Class, COUNT(SessionID) AS Attended, SUM(Minutes) AS TotalMinutes
FROM Sessions
WHERE Status = 'Attended'
GROUP BY Class
ORDER BY TotalMinutes DESC
```

Result:

| Class | Attended | TotalMinutes |
|---|---|---|
| Boxing | 3 | 150 |
| Yoga | 2 | 120 |
| Spin | 2 | 90 |

Trap: without the WHERE, Yoga (180) and Spin (135) would rank wrongly above Boxing.

questions.title: Café drinks report
questions.stimulus:
A café stores its menu and orders in a relational database. The contents of the Menu and Orders tables are shown.

**Menu**

| ItemID | ItemName | Category | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | Latte | Drink | 5.00 |
| I2 | Muffin | Food | 4.50 |
| I3 | Tea | Drink | 4.00 |
| I4 | Toastie | Food | 9.00 |
| I5 | Mocha | Drink | 5.50 |

**Orders**

| OrderID | ItemID | Qty |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | I1 | 2 |
| O2 | I2 | 1 |
| O3 | I3 | 3 |
| O4 | I1 | 1 |
| O5 | I4 | 2 |
| O6 | I5 | 1 |
| O7 | I3 | 1 |
| O8 | I2 | 4 |

parts.prompt:
The café manager wants the following report.

| Drink | NumberSold |
|---|---|
| Tea | 4 |
| Latte | 3 |
| Mocha | 1 |

Write an SQL query that produces this result.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct SQL query with at least TWO of: joining the tables; restricting to drinks; SUM with GROUP BY; renaming the columns and ordering
Shows some understanding of joining or grouping

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Menu.ItemName AS Drink, SUM(Orders.Qty) AS NumberSold
FROM Menu, Orders
WHERE Menu.ItemID = Orders.ItemID
  AND Menu.Category = 'Drink'
GROUP BY Menu.ItemID
ORDER BY NumberSold DESC
```

Traps: the report only contains drinks (WHERE Category = 'Drink'); NumberSold is the total quantity (SUM(Qty)), not the number of orders (COUNT would give Tea 2, Latte 2); both headings are renamed.
